questions.q: ___ I want is a good night's sleep.
questions.explanation: A wh-cleft starts with 'what' + clause + 'is'.

questions.q: It was John ___ broke the vase.
questions.explanation: An it-cleft for a person uses 'who' (or 'that').
A wh-cleft emphasises the thing with 'what'.

options: It was in 1999 what they got married.
It was in 1999 that they got married.
It was in 1999 which they got married.
That was in 1999 that they got married.
questions.explanation: An it-cleft emphasises the time with 'it was ... that'.

questions.q: It was the manager ___ approved the plan.
questions.explanation: An it-cleft for a person takes 'who'.
A wh-cleft names the activity with 'what'.

questions.q: It was yesterday ___ I saw her.
questions.explanation: An it-cleft for time uses 'that'.

options: That surprised me was his reaction.
Which surprised me was his reaction.
What surprised me was his reaction.
What surprised me it was his reaction.
questions.explanation: A wh-cleft puts 'what' before the verb phrase.

questions.q: All ___ he wants is peace and quiet.
questions.explanation: 'All (that)' starts an emphatic cleft sentence.

questions.q: It was his attitude ___ annoyed me.
questions.explanation: An it-cleft for a thing uses 'that'.
A wh-cleft emphasises the subject with 'what'.

options: It was the children who made all the noise.
It was the children which made all the noise.
It were the children who made all the noise.
It was the children that they made all the noise.
questions.explanation: An it-cleft for people uses 'who'.

questions.q: It was to Sarah ___ I spoke.
questions.explanation: An it-cleft can emphasise a prepositional phrase with 'that'.

questions.q: ___ I don't understand is why he left.
questions.explanation: A wh-cleft starts with 'what' for the unknown thing.

options: That I need is a holiday.
What I need is a holiday.
Which I need is a holiday.
What I need it is a holiday.
questions.explanation: A wh-cleft follows the pattern 'what + clause + is'.

questions.q: It was the exam ___ worried her most.
questions.explanation: An it-cleft for a thing takes 'that'.
'All that' introduces an emphatic cleft.

options: It was only after the war that he returned home.
It was only after the war what he returned home.
It was only after the war which he returned home.
That was only after the war that he returned home.
questions.explanation: An it-cleft emphasises the time clause with 'it was ... that'.
A wh-cleft with 'do' emphasises the action.

options: It wasn't the money what mattered, it was the gesture.
It wasn't the money which mattered, it was the gesture.
It wasn't the money that mattered, it was the gesture.
That wasn't the money that mattered, it was the gesture.
questions.explanation: A negative it-cleft contrasts two elements with 'that'.
